behaviors.behavior: TransformOp repeatedly searches transformation options while the policy has budget and performance is not satisfied.
behaviors.precondition: A transformation policy P with HasBudget and PerfNotSatisfied is provided.

behaviors.behavior: For each transformation option, TransformOp initializes an empty sub-operator list S.
behaviors.precondition: Inside the transformation-option loop body of TransformOp.

behaviors.behavior: TransformOp obtains the operator's m input TeSAs and single output TeSA via InputsOutputsTeSAOf(N).
behaviors.precondition: Operator N has m inputs and a single output.

behaviors.behavior: For each input i in 1..m, TransformOp transforms input TeSA Ii using the policy's TransformTeSA to produce a set Ti.
behaviors.precondition: Operator N has m inputs.

behaviors.behavior: TransformOp transforms the output TeSA O using the policy's TransformTeSA to produce a set To.
behaviors.precondition: After transforming inputs.

behaviors.behavior: TransformOp iterates over the Cartesian product T1×...×Tm×To of decomposed input and output TeSAs.
behaviors.precondition: Each Ti and To contains one or more transformed TeSAs.

behaviors.behavior: For each Cartesian-product tuple, TransformOp creates a sub-operator Nsub by SpecializeOp with the original op N and the tuple's input/output TeSAs.
behaviors.precondition: Iterating over T1×...×Tm×To.

behaviors.behavior: TransformOp appends each specialized sub-operator to the sub-operator list S.
behaviors.precondition: A sub-operator Nsub has been created.

behaviors.behavior: TransformOp composes the sub-operators of S into a graph G.
behaviors.precondition: Sub-operator list S for the current option is complete.

behaviors.behavior: TransformOp profiles the composed graph G on real hardware.
behaviors.precondition: Graph G has been composed from S.

behaviors.behavior: TransformOp records the profiled performance result via the policy's RecordPerf.
behaviors.precondition: Graph G has been profiled.

behaviors.behavior: TransformOp returns the best transformation selected by the policy after the search loop.
behaviors.precondition: Search loop has terminated.

behaviors.behavior: The operator is transformed into |To| times the product over m inputs of |Ti| sub-operators, the Cartesian product of decomposed TeSAs.
behaviors.precondition: Inputs and output TeSAs are each decomposed into one or more TeSAs.

evidence.quote: the operator is transformed to|To| ∏m i=1|Ti| sub-operators, which are the Cartesian product of those decomposed TeSAs.

behaviors.behavior: Each sub-operator is assumed to have the same computation logic as the original operator (e.g., expressible with Einstein summation).
behaviors.precondition: The original operator's computation can be expressed in the assumed form.

evidence.quote: The sub-operator usually has the same computation logic as the original operator

behaviors.behavior: P::TransformTeSA(T) initializes an empty transformed list Ttransformed and returns a new transformation option per run.
behaviors.precondition: P::TransformTeSA(T) is called.

evidence.quote: /* return a new transformation option per run */

behaviors.behavior: TransformTeSA first applies BitRounding to T using a sampled bit option, producing k intermediate TeSAs T1..Tk.
behaviors.precondition: Hardware-supported bit widths determine the sampled option.

behaviors.behavior: For each BitRounding result Ti, TransformTeSA applies WeightedBlockCover to produce j TeSAs and extends them into Ttransformed.
behaviors.precondition: For each i in 1..k.

evidence.quote: Ttrans f ormed.Extend(T 1 i , . . . ,T j i );

behaviors.behavior: TransformTeSA returns the accumulated list Ttransformed of transformed TeSAs.
behaviors.precondition: All k BitRounding results have been processed.

behaviors.behavior: A regular sparsity pattern is defined as a TeSA showing only one type of quantization attribute and one block size of pruning attribute.
behaviors.precondition: Used as the target of the transformation pass.

evidence.quote: a regular sparsity pattern means the TeSA of a tensor shows only one type of quantization attribute and one block size of pruning attribute.

behaviors.behavior: The transformation may choose not to decompose a tensor and select block size 1x1, indicating fine-grained sparsity that is hard to regularize.
behaviors.precondition: The policy decides against decomposition.

evidence.quote: the algorithm may decide not to decompose a tensor and choose a block size of 1x1, indicating that the TeSA has a ﬁne-grained sparsity that is hard to be transformed to regular sparsity.

behaviors.behavior: The execution-plan transformation for a DNN model is performed operator-by-operator.
behaviors.precondition: A DNN model with multiple operators.

evidence.quote: The detailed execution plan transformation for a DNN model is performed operator-by-operator, shown in Algo-rithm 3.
